segments.label: Contractual write-off
segments.sub: The provider erases the gap between sticker price and the plan's allowed amount — the patient never owes it.

segments.label: Insurance paid
segments.sub: What Blue Cross actually sent the provider.

segments.label: Patient owed
segments.sub: Deductible plus 10% in-network coinsurance — the patient's real out-of-pocket.

patientShareNote: Of $4,506 in real professional charges over eight years, the patient's own share was $631.87 — about 14% — the small deductible-and-coinsurance amounts the plan assigns. More than half the sticker price ($2343.69) simply vanished as contractual write-off the patient never sees.

reconciliation.note: Insurance-paid + contractual write-off + patient-owed = net billed, to the penny.
reconciliation.aggregationNote: Anchored on the per-claim remittance (the closed claims that actually adjudicated). Epic's transaction-match log shows a larger 'payment' figure ($2,162.31) because it records gross postings before the deductible is shifted to the patient; that log is not the insurer's net-paid and is not used here.
